question.prompt: A player chooses one of the numbers \(1\) through \(4.\) After the choice has been made, two regular four-sided (tetrahedral) dice are rolled, with the sides of the dice numbered \(1\) through \(4.\) If the number chosen appears on the bottom of exactly one die after it is rolled, then the player wins \(\$1.\) If the number chosen appears on the bottom of both of the dice, then the player wins \(\$2.\) If the number chosen does not appear on the bottom of either of the dice, the player loses \(\$1.\) What is the expected return to the player, in dollars, for one roll of the dice?

solutions.explanation:
Whatever number is chosen, each die has one matching face and three nonmatching faces. Distinguish the two dice, so their rolls give \(4\cdot4=16\) equally likely ordered outcomes.

There are \(3\cdot3=9\) outcomes with no match. Exactly one match occurs in \(1\cdot3+3\cdot1=6\) outcomes, according to which die matches. Both dice match in \(1\) outcome. These cases are disjoint and account for all \(9+6+1=16\) outcomes.

Treat a gain as positive and a loss as negative. The expected return is the probability-weighted average payoff:
\[
(-1)\frac9{16}+1\frac6{16}+2\frac1{16}
=\frac{-9+6+2}{16}
=-\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus the expected return is \(-\frac1{16}\) dollar, choice \(B\).
solutions.title: Average the payoffs over the outcomes
